definitions.explanation: A trick performed by a magician using sleight of hand or props. Literally means 'hand skill' or 'hand technique'.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{手品|てじな}が{上手|じょうず}だ。
{子供|こども}たちの{前|まえ}で{手品|てじな}を{見|み}せた。
examples.english: I showed magic tricks in front of the children.

examples.japanese: トランプの{手品|てじな}を{教|おし}えてくれませんか。
examples.english: Could you teach me a card trick?

notes:
USAGE: {手品|てじな} refers to close-up magic or sleight of hand tricks. It's the everyday word for magic tricks, while マジック is also commonly used as a loanword.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{手品|てじな}をする (to do a magic trick)
・{手品|てじな}を{見|み}せる (to show a magic trick)
・{手品|てじな}を{披露|ひろう}する (to perform magic - formal)
・{手品師|てじなし} (magician)

RELATED WORDS:
・マジック (magic - loanword, more general)
・{魔法|まほう} (magic - supernatural, not tricks)
・{奇術|きじゅつ} (magic arts - more formal)
・{手品師|てじなし}/マジシャン (magician)

Note: {手品|てじな} implies skill and technique rather than supernatural power, unlike {魔法|まほう}.
